passage: Creche note, Tuesday. Around midday, Farhan, two, began rubbing his eyes with both fists and tugging his left ear. He also pressed his face into my shoulder. I didn't decide from one sign. It was just before nap time, he had eaten his lunch well, he felt cool to touch, and the room had been noisy since morning. I took him to the quiet corner and he slept. If the ear-tugging keeps going or worries us, I will tell his parents to see the doctor. 🙂 Ganga

qa.q: When did Farhan start rubbing his eyes and tugging his ear?
qa.a: Around midday, just before nap time.

qa.q: What might Farhan have been feeling when he rubbed his eyes and tugged his ear, and how did Ganga decide?
qa.a: He was most likely tired, since it was just before nap time and he pressed his face into Ganga's shoulder, and Ganga checked the whole picture: lunch eaten, cool skin and a noisy room. The ear tug could have another cause, so Ganga will watch whether it continues.

qa.q: What should Ganga do if the ear tugging continues?
qa.a: Ganga should tell his parents so they can check with the doctor, since it may be more than tiredness.

qa.q: How might Farhan's parents feel on reading the note?
qa.a: They may feel reassured that Ganga looked carefully and told them, and know what to watch for.

grounding: A toddler rubs his eyes and pulls his ear, an ambiguous cue that the caregiver checks against the whole situation.

passage: The bus ride from town had taken all afternoon, and by the evening meal Avni, two, was tugging at her right ear and rubbing her eyes with her fists. Jomon looked at her: she had eaten little, the radio was loud and she had been awake since dawn. He turned the radio off, lifted her on his lap and rocked her. She pressed her face into his shirt and was asleep in a few minutes. He decided that if the tugging carried on the next day, he would ask the clinic nurse.

qa.q: What did Jomon think Avni's ear tugging and eye rubbing meant?
qa.a: He thought she was tired after the long bus ride, since she had eaten little and been awake since dawn. He still kept in mind that ear tugging can have other causes.

qa.q: What would Jomon do if the tugging kept going?
qa.a: He would ask the clinic nurse the next day, as it might be something more than tiredness.

qa.q: How might Avni have felt when he turned off the radio?
qa.a: She may have felt relieved as the noise stopped, and safe in his lap. 🙂

grounding: A toddler rubs eyes and tugs an ear when sleepy, and an adult checks the wider context instead of relying on one sign.
